An interface between academic rigor and practice.

FieldCompanies bring the problem, the data and the access.
CasesThe story, written so that others can decide.
PapersThe mechanism, proved and peer-reviewed. A slower, inner loop: a paper takes far longer than a case.
ClassroomThe test: can people who run businesses use the idea?
BookAt the tip: the framework, written for practice. It starts the next loop.

2003: four competitors in one room (among 70 others) at INSEAD. I was there as a PhD student.

2003The EU WEEE Directive makes producers responsible for their electronic waste.
2003–05HP, Electrolux, Sony and P&G design the European Recycling Platform (ERP) in workshops at INSEAD.
2005ERP launches in Austria. Within a year, recycling fees fall by 85%

The field moved first. The papers came later.

Inside two papers: who should be responsible, and how to keep rivals together.

2012Atasu & Subramanian · Production and Operations Management

Extended Producer Responsibility for E-Waste: Individual or Collective Producer Responsibility?

Individual

Design for recovery

2016Gui, Atasu, Ergun & Toktay · Management Science

Efficient Implementation of Collective Extended Producer Responsibility Legislation

Tested on data from Washington State’s programme

The first paper asked which system to choose. The second asked how to keep a collective system together: the question any coalition of rivals faces.

Inside three papers: if remanufacturing pays, why don’t firms do more of it?

2008Atasu, Sarvary & Van Wassenhove · Management Science

Remanufacturing as a Marketing Strategy

Remanufacturing pays above thresholds for:

Cost savings
Green segment
Market growth
Value of remanufactured products

Under competition, it can defend market share through price discrimination.

Theory, motivated by Apple and HP products; later shared with Apple

2015Agrawal, Atasu & Van Ittersum · Management Science

Remanufacturing, Third-Party Competition, and Consumers’ Perceived Value of New Products

Behavioural experiments

2018Kovach, Atasu & Banerjee · Production and Operations Management

Salesforce Incentives and Remanufacturing

Commission on total revenue

New
Remanufactured

“You are ruining us.”

Too few remanufactured sales, possibly none, even when remanufacturing costs almost nothing.

Separate commission rates: remanufacturing pays in more cases.

The first model said when remanufacturing pays. The experiments showed what it does to the value of new products. The incentives paper helped explain why firms still did not do it.

What the loops left behind: a framework, and a book.

Move 1 · Make the caseWhy must we act, and why now?Teaching: the tragedy of the commons, applied in sustainability classes.
Move 2 · Redefine valueWhere can we create value that also pays?Classroom discussions that produced the four-stakeholder framework used in NPV Plus; the NPV Plus loop, Malta (2018) to SMCP (2025).
Move 3 · Recognize constraintsWhy is that value hard to capture?My research career: in operations, the devil is in the detail. Six constraints, next.
Move 4 · Reinvent the businessWhich partners, models and technologies unlock it?Three keys:
Key 1 · PartnersNew partners, even rivals.The ERP loop: 2003 to Zirq (2024).
Key 2 · Business modelsKeep ownership, and products come back.The remanufacturing loop: 2006 to the HBR article (2021).
Key 3 · TechnologyInvent it, invent it for others, or borrow it.Recycling technology and producer responsibility (2021); EcoVadis case (2024).
The engineRepresentation, incentives, experimentation.The Paris 2024 loop; salesforce incentives (2018).

A summary of what these projects had in common: a starting point, not a result.

© 2027 Atalay Atasu. All rights reserved.

The framework in one picture.

Move 1 · Make the casePressure reaches the business through four stakeholders.
Move 2 · Redefine valueMeasure the value in a language finance accepts: NPV Plus.
Move 3 · Recognize constraintsSix constraints open a gap between value on paper and value captured.
Move 4 · Reinvent the businessPartners, business models and technology close part of the gap.
The engineRepresentation, incentives and experimentation keep it running.

Tilos, through the framework.

1Make the caseBeaches feed the economy.
2Redefine valueClean beaches are worth more than the system costs: twice the cost, and still worth it.
3Recognize constraintsNothing works unless every household and business sorts at source.
4Reinvent the businessResidents and tourists as partners; a zero-waste service, not waste management.
The engineLocal champions, visible results per household, constant pilots.

These are the loops that closed.

Almost all those papers were rejected at least once.

Many conversations with companies went nowhere.

Where most of the loops that closed began

With a participant in an MBA, GEMBA or executive education class: someone who heard our applied work and came to trust the legitimacy of the institution behind it.

In my experience, the classroom has been the most reliable door.

What I would tell my younger self
Spend time in the classroom.Participants who trust the institution have opened most of the doors.
Write the case early.It is the first record of the problem, and an early test of whether the story holds.
Teach it.If people who run businesses can use the idea, it is more likely to travel.
Then work out the mechanism in a paper.And expect rejection, more than once.
